data.title: Gold edges higher but falls for the week on hawkish Fed expectations
data.description:
Gold futures snapped a four-session losing streak Friday but ended with a weekly loss as a stronger dollar, surging Treasury yields, and growing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates again next month weighed on the metal.

U.S. Treasury yields posted multiyear highs this week, with the two-year, 10-year, and 20-year yields all rising sharply to end at 4.862%, 5.180%, and 5.500%, respectively.

"Investment metals faced a bond-market stress test, with surging Treasury yields supporting a stronger dollar and raising the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets," Saxo Bank analysts said in a note.

The ⁠Fed raised interest rates by a quarter-point last week, its first increase in three years, and traders are pricing in a 66% chance of an October hike and a 93% chance of an increase in December, according to CME's FedWatch ​Tool.

Front-month Comex gold for September delivery added 0.5% on Friday to $4,286.20/oz, and front-month Comex September silver climbed 1.2% to $64.245/oz; for the week, gold and silver fell 2.3% and 3.5%, respectively.

data.title: Northrop Grumman's strategic deterrent deal gets $111.4M boost
data.description:
Key points:
  • Northrop Grumman's system unit announced on Friday that it received a ~$111.4M contract modification for the Ground-Based Strategic Deterrent engineering, manufacturing, and early production program.

data.title: 13D Filings — Barrons.com
data.description:
These disclosures are from 13Ds filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission. 13Ds are filed within 10 days of an entity's attaining more than 5% in any class of a company's securities. Subsequent changes in holdings or intentions must be reported in amended filings. This material is from Sept. 17 through Sept. 23, 2026. Source: VerityData

Activist Filings

Vail Resorts (MTN) DKR Oasis Management filed an initial 13D regarding its stake in the mountain resort operator, shifting to the stance of an activist investor from previous disclosures in a passive 13G. Oasis reported that it purchased 891,059 Vail Resorts shares from Sept. 3 through Sept. 18 at per share prices ranging from $136 to $140.26, after selling 596,765 shares from July 16 through Sept. 4 at $135.08 to $150.21.

On Sept. 10, Oasis notified Vail Resorts of its intent to nominate four director candidates at the 2026 annual meeting, including Robert Chapek and retired Olympic athlete Picabo Street.

Oasis said it believes Vail's portfolio of 42 mountain resorts is not fully reflected in its valuation relative to peers, and that a reconstituted board would sharpen the company's focus on guest experience, pricing strategy, marketing effectiveness, and fuller use of its hospitality assets.

Following the latest activity, Oasis Management owns 2,623,912 Vail Resorts shares, or 7.4% of those outstanding. Shares of Vail Resorts have gained just 4% in value in 2026.

Increases in Holdings

Dynatrace (DT) Pictet Asset Management raised its stake in the information-technology infrastructure software company to 14,564,509 shares. Pictet Asset Management reported that it purchased 152,807 Dynatrace shares from Sept. 11 through Sept. 15 at per share prices ranging from $51.07 to $55.17, and sold 21,821 shares from Sept. 9 through Sept. 15 at $50.60 to $53.34.

Following the latest activity, Pictet Asset Management once again owns a 5% stake in Dynatrace's outstanding stock, placing Pictet back above the reporting threshold after it dipped below that level earlier this month. Shares of Dynatrace have gained approximately 39.2% in value in 2026.

Decreases in Holdings

Genco Shipping & Trading (GNK) Diana Shipping lowered its stake in the dry-bulk shipping company to 2,178,585 shares. Diana Shipping did so through the sale of 205,000 Genco Shipping & Trading shares from Sept. 14 through Sept. 15 at per share prices ranging from $26.86 to $28.21.

Following the latest sales, Diana Shipping continues to own a 4.9% stake in Genco Shipping & Trading's outstanding stock, placing Diana Shipping below the 5% threshold that would require it to report further sales. Shares of Genco have gained roughly 42.2% in value in 2026.

Talos Energy (TALO) Carlos Slim lowered his stake in the oil-and-gas company to 39,079,036 shares. The Mexican billionaire did so through the sale of 1,381,000 Talos Energy shares on Sept. 15 at per share prices ranging from $18.49 to $18.66.

Following the latest sales, Carlos Slim continues to own a 23.4% stake in Talos Energy's outstanding stock. Shares of Talos Energy have gained roughly 47.3% in value in 2026.

data.title: Strive preferred stock trades enough to buy 1,400 Bitcoin worth $117M
data.description:
Strive, Inc. has figured out a way to buy Bitcoin without taking on debt, without heavily diluting shareholders, and without touching a convertible note. The vehicle is a perpetual preferred stock called SATA, and it traded enough volume this week to fund the purchase of roughly 1,400 Bitcoin worth around $117 million.

Strive launched its Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Preferred Stock, ticker SATA, in November 2025. The IPO was oversubscribed, bringing in between $149 million and $160 million at launch.

The mechanics are straightforward: SATA carries a $100 par value and pays a variable annualized dividend of roughly 13%. Whenever shares trade at or above that par value, Strive activates an at-the-market program to issue new shares and capture the proceeds. Those proceeds go directly into Bitcoin.

Between August 31 and September 4, 2026, Strive purchased 1,375 BTC for approximately $109 million. About 70% of that capital, roughly $92 million, came directly from SATA share sales. That purchase averaged approximately $79,281 per Bitcoin and pushed Strive's total holdings to 24,531 BTC.

Then, between September 8 and September 11, Strive made another move: 469 BTC for $36.6 million, this time entirely funded by SATA. That transaction brought the company to exactly 25,000 BTC in total holdings.

It also pushed SATA's notional value past $1.04 billion. A preferred stock instrument that launched less than a year ago has already crossed the ten-figure mark in notional terms.

Strive held Bitcoin only in the low thousands when it completed its merger in January 2026. CEO Matt Cole has publicly highlighted what the company calls its amplification ratio, which measures how much Bitcoin NAV the company controls relative to the preferred equity it has issued.

The broader Bitcoin treasury playbook was popularized by MicroStrategy, which used convertible debt and equity raises to accumulate Bitcoin on its balance sheet.

Perpetual preferred equity does not mature. There is no principal repayment deadline, no covenant that kicks in if Bitcoin falls 30%. The dividend obligation is real, but it does not trigger the same existential risk that debt maturities can create.

SATA's target trading band is $99 to $101 per share. As long as it stays in that range, the system keeps feeding itself. High trading volumes in the first half of September 2026 demonstrated that the instrument can absorb capital influxes large enough to move Bitcoin purchasing power by hundreds of BTC per week.
